requirements.text: The umbrella will be a web-based menu system allowing the user to choose between the games.
The umbrella will be a singular component, providing links to projects relating to fractions, decimals, and percents in a format accessible over the World Wide Web.
An introductory movie to set up the storyline.
A main menu, including a brief help section.
A series of fraction questions (testing arithmetic, equivalence, graphical interpretation, and improper versus proper fraction skills) that sequentially form a storyline related to the introduction.
An ending scene where the user's score is calculated and ranked, with an option to quit the game or try again.
A component accessible over the World Wide Web will allow the series of fraction questions to be updated by an administrator of the game.
The user's score must be kept as local data within the game so that the results may be given at the end of the game.
Input will consist entirely of mouse clicks for the user to choose answer options and to set preferences.
Output will be sounds and animations through Flash movies to acknowledge success or failure in answering the fraction questions.
There is an option to skip the introduction, if desired.
No portion of the interface will require the keyboard; all input will be accomplished via mouse clicks.
The component will generate a text file on the game server, which is used by the game sequence to dynamically load question data.
The component opens the specified S2S product in a separate window.
The Question Updater must implement secure authentication, including password hashing (e.g., bcrypt or Argon2) and transmission over HTTPS to prevent credential interception.

The server-side script responsible for updating the question text file must implement strict input validation, sanitization, and file path restriction to prevent unauthorized file modification or code injection.
The product must implement independent security controls for administrative access and data integrity, rather than relying solely on the client-side browser environment.
Define reliability by specifying a maximum allowable failure rate or a requirement for error handling during network interruptions or Flash plugin crashes.
Specify that administrative access must be protected by secure authentication (e.g., HTTPS/TLS) and rate-limiting to prevent unauthorized modification of game data.
Explicitly define the storage mechanism for local data and specify how the system should behave if the local storage is cleared or inaccessible.
The main game component shall begin playback within 30 seconds on a standard 56kbps modem connection.
Updates made via the Question Updater shall be reflected in the game sequence within 5 seconds of successful submission.

OPEN: The performance requirement assumes a 'regular modem connection' but does not define the expected concurrent user load or server-side latency requirements for the Question Updater. - Define the maximum number of concurrent users the server must support and the maximum acceptable latency for loading question data files.

OPEN: The PRD does not define the expected concurrent user load for the web server hosting the game and the question updater. - The web server shall support at least 30 concurrent users accessing the game and question updater without exceeding a 2-second response time for interactive elements.
